items.title: Doctors want liability shield from AI mistakes
items.excerpt: The American Medical Association adopted policy calling for federal and state legislation shielding physicians from liability when AI products injure patients despite intended use, and for laws requiring AI vendors to carry liability insurance and disclose performance data.
items.rationale: Policy/liability axis: AMA formally adopted a legislative ask that would shift AI-injury liability onto vendors (insurance + performance disclosure) — concrete new position, assigned to politics only.

items.title: Court allows news publishers' copyright lawsuit against OpenAI to go ahead
items.excerpt: The Ontario Court of Appeal dismissed OpenAI's appeal of a jurisdiction ruling, letting Canadian news publishers' copyright suit over ChatGPT training proceed in Ontario rather than a U.S. court.
items.rationale: Copyright litigation axis: an appellate ruling (11-13) keeps a training-data copyright suit in Canadian courts; off-list outlet accepted as CP wire of a primary ruling — note the Star is a plaintiff, writer should attribute neutrally.

items.title: Indonesia's new copyright bill would force Google and Meta to pay to aggregate news
items.excerpt: Meta, TikTok and Google testified in Indonesia's parliament against a copyright bill that would make platforms pay publishers for previews, including in AI search products, and when journalism is used to train AI models — which would make Indonesia the first Southeast Asian country to fold AI into copyright law.
items.rationale: Bill axis: a pending national copyright bill that would require payment for AI training and AI-search previews — first in Southeast Asia; new jurisdiction, not covered before.

items.title: 말레이, 앨리스 황 근무 메가스피드 자회사 AI반도체 유출 조사
items.excerpt: 말레이시아 투자통상산업부가 메가스피드 인터내셔널의 자회사 스피드매트릭스가 첨단 AI 반도체를 다른 국가로 유출했는지 공식 조사에 착수했다고 밝혔다.
items.rationale: Geopolitics axis: the only Nvidia/Megaspeed saga item carrying a new official action — Malaysia's trade ministry opened a formal investigation; the saga is limited to this one card today.

items.title: Whitehall to increase face-to-face job interviews after surge in AI applications
items.excerpt: In the most extreme cases, civil service leaders suspect that entire applications — including interviewees on a video calls — were generated by AI.
items.rationale: Policy axis (government rules on AI use): the UK civil service is changing its recruitment process — more in-person interviews — in direct response to AI-generated applications; delete AI and there is no story. Writer should attribute the 'entire applications generated by AI' suspicion to civil service leaders, not assert it.

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR2026111311.new_action: Malaysia's Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry opened a formal investigation into Megaspeed subsidiary Speedmatrix over diversion of advanced AI chips (new government investigation, distinct from the US SE-Asia licensing move of 11-13 and the 11-07 congressional summons).
